title: Greenland-minus-Pacific seasonal SST trends were uncertain in two products for 1983-2024
abstract: We tested whether the June-August minus prior December-February sea surface temperature (SST) difference increased more south of Greenland than in a North Pacific box at 50-60 N. We used fixed regional averages from ERSSTv5 and COBE-SST2. For 1983-2024, the Greenland-minus-Pacific trend was -0.1299 C per decade in ERSSTv5 and -0.0997 in COBE-SST2. The paired 95% five-year residual block intervals were -0.3112 to 0.0552 and -0.2643 to 0.0677. Thus neither product gave a clear regional difference. A planned check ending in 2022 gave negative nominal intervals in both products. Adding 2023-2024 moved the paired slopes toward zero by 0.0964 and 0.0830 C per decade. An exact descriptive decomposition linked this change to higher Greenland and lower Pacific seasonal-contrast slopes. Three- and ten-year blocks, shifted seasons, and 58 N bounds left the main difference uncertain. This comparison adds a Pacific reference and COBE-SST2 to prior campaign work on Greenland. Shared input observations, unequal spatial support, revised reconstructions, short residual blocks and time-window dependence limit inference. The test does not establish equal trends or a physical cause. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, slope draws, two figures and source hashes. Raw fields and monthly series remain external.

display.caption: Regional JJA minus prior DJF SST and paired trend intervals for 1983-2024. Thin lines are annual values; thick lines are centered seven-year means. Fits use unsmoothed annual values.

All planned paired Greenland-minus-Pacific checks. Intervals use paired residual blocks. Check intervals are nominal and are not adjusted for multiple checks. Only the 1983-2022 check excludes zero in both products.

citations.reason: Uses the same Greenland bounds and ERSST source snapshot. Adds a paired Pacific comparison, COBE-SST2, and explicit endpoint analysis. No code reused.
Prior global study of seasonal SST amplification and its causes. Our regional contrast and uncertainty procedure differ.
